2. The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that the petitioner and 1st respondent are Hindus and their families are related.
The aggrieved person's maternal home is at Vishakapatnam, Andhra Pradesh.
The proposal of the 1st respondent was brought the 1st respondent's maternal grandfather in the early part of 2003.
The families of the aggrieved person and the 1st respondent along with aggrieved person and 1st respondent met in Hyderabad in August 2013 to discuss the marriage proposal and the alliance was fixed.
However the respondents 1 to 3 made an exorbitant dowry demand and finally the aggrieved person's family was constrained to agree to pay a dowry of Rs.61,00,000/- in various forms to the respondent.

It is submitted that since the families of the aggrieved person and respondents were related, the aggrieved person's father was constrained to agree to the dowry demand fearing breakdown in the family relations.

After the marriage alliance was fixed, the respondents 1 to 3 called the aggrieved person and her family informing them that the 1st respondent had got a seat in Oxford, London and hence the marriage had to be performed before he left United Kingdom.
As such the aggrieved person's parents and the aggrieved person came to Bangalore in August 2003 to finalize the marriage date and other details.

At that time, 1st respondent and his parents demanded that the residential flat in Vishakapatnam standing in the name of the aggrieved person's father should be transferred to their name as consideration of the marriage.
At that time the said flat was worth around Rs.15,00,000/-.
Though the aggrieved person's father was not keen to transfer it to their name, it was agreed that the same would be transferred into the aggrieved person's name.
The marriage was fixed on 8th September 2003 at ISCKON Bangalore and all arrangements and expenses for the same were borne by the aggrieved person's father.
This was also one of the conditions imposed by the respondents 1 to 3 as a condition for agreeing to go ahead with the marriage.
The respondents 1 to 3 had also demanded a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- for the purchase of a car,
The aggrieved person's father gave the respondents 1 to 3 a sum of Rs.14,00,000/- and another amount of Rs.10,00,000/- (Rupees ten lakhs only) by cash for purchase of gold.
That apart, the aggrieved person's parents also incurred expenditure for purchase of gold and jewelry to be given to the respondents and their relations.

The aggrieved person and 1st respondent were married as per Hindu rites and customs on 8th September 2003 at ISCKON Bangalore and the same was registered under the provisions of the Hindu marriage Act on 15th September 2003 before the Registrar of Marriages, Jayanagar,
Bangalore.
The copy of the marriage certificate and the wedding photograph is produced herewith as Document No 4 and 5.
As stated earlier all the expenses for the marriage was borne by the aggrieved person's father.
The aggrieved person's father incurred the entire expenses of around Rs.10,00,000/- for the conduct of the marriage.
The 1st respondent went to Chennai for his interview but for some reason not disclosed to the aggrieved person, his visa was rejected.
The aggrieved person and 1st respondent then left for the reception in Vishakaptnam.

Since the aggrieved person's father did not want the aggrieved person to undergo any discomfort in her matrimonial home, he arranged for the honeymoon to Singapore and Malaysia by incurring an expenditure of around Rs.2,40,000/-
(Rupees two lakhs forty thousand only).
After the aggrieved person and 1st respondent returned from the reception, they left for their honeymoon in November 2003.
During the honeymoon, the 1st respondent would constantly lei to the aggrieved person on trivial issues and would pick up flights on trivial issues.
However since the aggrieved person was newly married, she chose to ignore these incidents hoping that things will improve after they settle down to lead a marital life.
The aggrieved person and 1st respondent returned to the matrimonial home in Bangalore at Jayanagar and started living with respondents 2 and 3.
Meanwhile there was a robbery and matrimonial house was burnt.
The 3rd respondent claimed that all the jewelry given to the petitioner at the time of the marriage worth Rs.10,00,000/- Was stolen in the said robbery.
After the said incident, the aggrieved person and respondents 1 to 3 shifted to a rented house in Jayanagar.

The aggrieved person's nightmare started as the respondents 1 to 3 would constantly shout and harass the aggrieved person for all trivial issues and would constantly come up with new monetary and dowry demands.

This continued for nearly a year and added to this harassment was the fact that the 1st respondent had left his job for joining Oxford and since the Oxford seat did not come through remained at home without a job for nearly one year.
The aggrieved person realized that she was pregnant around January 2004 and since she had medical complications, she was advised bed rest for the entire term of the pregnancy.
The respondents 1 to 3 insisted that they could not look after the aggrieved person and demanded that the aggrieved person's mother join them to look after the aggrieved person for some time.
However after few days, the aggrieved person's mother left, the harassment meted out by the 3rd respondent increased and it also lead to fights in the family.
The 3rd respondent claimed that she was angry with the 1st respondent and demanded that the aggrieved person and the 1st respondent leave the matrimonial home.
The aggrieved person's parents had to come from Vishakapatnam and had to take the aggrieved person and the 1st respondent to Vishakapatnam as they did not have any place to stay.
Meanwhile the 1st respondent secured a job in Hyderabad at TATA teleservices and consequently the aggrieved person and 1st respondent moved to Hyderabad.

However the 3rd respondent was not happy with the said move and started harassing the aggrieved person over phone and instigating the 1st respondent, who would then harass and torture the aggrieved person.

This harassment and torture went on for years and even continues as on date.

He would resent any demand for money for household expenses and even money to celebrate the minor daughter's birthday.

The 1st respondent would prevent the aggrieved person from inviting any friends and children for the minor daughter's birthday and would threaten to create a scene and abuse guests if the aggrieved person invited any one for the birthday or even had a birthday party.

However things turned dangerous when in December 2011, the aggrieved person came to know that the 1st respondent had been video taping the aggrieved person while she was having bath or changing clothes.
The 1st respondent started spiking the aggrieved person's tea and medicines with sleeping pills and would molest and film the aggrieved person without her knowledge and consent.

3. After registration of the case, summons was issued to the respondents and they appeared through their counsel and filed detailed statement of objection denying each and every allegations made against them.
4. In order to substantiate their respective contentions, the petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.
The respondent got examined himself as R.W.1 and got marked 22 documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.22.

5. Heard arguments on both the sides, perused the petition, objection and available materials on record.
6.
The following points would arise for my consideration.

1. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the relief's as sought in the petition?
2. What order?

7. On perusal of materials before this court, My findings on the above said points are as under:
1. POINT No.1: PARTLY IN THE AFFIRMATIVE 2. POINT No.2: AS PER FINAL ORDER For the following REASONS 8. POINT No.1:

To file a petition U/s.12 of the Act, it is necessary that the petitioner has to establish two things firstly, she must establish that, the petitioner and respondent or respondents lived or are living together, in a domestic relationship.
Secondly, that the respondent or respondents have subjected her to acts of domestic violence.

To prove the domestic relationship the petitioner is required to prove that she and the respondents have lived together in a relationship of marriage or in a relationship in the nature of marriage or related by consanguinity or adoption or as family members living together as a joint family.
To prove the act of domestic violence the petitioner is required o prove any one or more of the acts committed by the respondent or respondents as contemplated U/s.3 of the Act.

This draws a presumption to this court at this stage that the petitioner earns about Rs.25 Lakhs p.a.
by the school which she runs.
Further she is residing in the apartment purchased by the respondent No.1, which draws a presumption that she has permanent residence in the said apartment.
In her cross-examination she has given admission that 1st respondent used to take her outing and other family functions.
The petitioner has admitted the photographs which were confronted to her during her cross-examination and the said photographs came to be marked as Ex.R.1.
On perusal of Ex.R.1 it is clear that respondents have not caused any harassment or torture to the petitioner, when she was residing in her marital home.
She further denies that the respondent No.2 and 3 has taken LIC policy in the name of petitioner's child.
Further she admits that the said LIC policy and the same came to be marked as Ex.R.2.
On perusal of the documents marked on behalf of the respondent it is clear that respondent No.1 to 3 have not harassed the petitioner in any manner.

If such is the case then the respondents would not had made LIC policy in the name of the petitioner's child and the photographs which were admitted by the petitioner gives the clear picture that petitioner has not approached this court with clean hands.

sentences.text: On perusal of these depositions it is clear that relationship between the petitioners and respondent is not in dispute.
The petitioners have failed to prove the respondent has harassed them.
However no specific allegations are being made against the respondents so as to prove the act of Domestic Violence.
Mere allegations which are not specific and which are vague in nature cannot be accepted as proof of Domestic Violence.
15. When such being the case, the infliction of domestic violence made against the respondents gets diluted and same cannot be accepted.
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 is beneficiary legislation and is intended to protect the interest of wife.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
In order to claim any relief under the said Act, must satisfy and prove before this Court that she is an aggrieved woman U/s.2(a)
of the said Act and she has been subjected to domestic violence as defined U/s.3 of Domestic violence Act.
Hence on perusal of the evidence of P.W.1 it establishes that except the vague allegations made against the respondent No.1, the petitioner has not proved her case of domestic violence against him.
16. The petitioner has sought for a protection order restraining the respondent from committing an act of Domestic Violence.
As discussed above there are no evidence to show that an act of Domestic Violence was committed by the respondent.
Hence this relief is liable to be declined.
17. The petitioner has sought for a residence order U/s.19 of Domestic Violence Act, directing the respondents to secure same level or alternative accommodation for petitioner.

On perusal of materials before this court, there is no evidence placed by the petitioner to prove the level of accommodation she enjoyed while she was residing with the respondent and the shared house hold.

Hence the said relief is liable to be declined.
18.
The petitioner has sought for an amount of Rs.2 crores as compensation and maintenance amount of Rs.40,000/- p.m.
Since the act of Domestic violence is not specifically proved before this Court granting compensation would be inappropriate.
But, the respondent No.1 is held responsible to pay compensation amount of Rs.3,00,000/- as the respondent No.1 being the husband of petitioner, he is also the father of the child.
It is his bound duty to look after the legally wedded wife and child born out of wedlock.
He has to discharge his duty as husband as well as a responsible father.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 PARTLY IN THE AFFIRMAIVE.
19. POINT No.2:

In view of the materials placed before this court, pleadings, depositions and documentary evidence, this court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005, is allowed in part.

opennyai_summary.facts:
1 This is a petition filed by the petitioner U/s.12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act,
2005 seeking relief's U/s.18, 19, 20 and 22 of the said Act.
The proposal of the 1st respondent was brought the 1st respondent's maternal grandfather in the early part of 2003.
The families of the aggrieved person and the 1st respondent along with aggrieved person and 1st respondent met in Hyderabad in August 2013 to discuss the marriage proposal and the alliance was fixed.
However the respondents 1 to 3 made an exorbitant dowry demand and finally the aggrieved person's family was constrained to agree to pay a dowry of Rs.61,00,000/- in various forms to the respondent.
The aggrieved person and 1st respondent were married as per Hindu rites and customs on 8th September 2003 at ISCKON Bangalore and the same was registered under the provisions of the Hindu marriage Act on 15th September 2003 before the Registrar of Marriages, Jayanagar,
Bangalore.
While filing the complaint, the aggrieved person was informed that the 1st respondent had filed a complaint against the aggrieved person on 15th May 2013 making false allegations that the aggrieved person was harassing the 1st respondent.
The aggrieved person was constrained to file a GWC 107/2013 seeking guardianship and custody of the child as the aggrieved person feared that the respondents Smt. B.N.A. Shilpa Lakshmi vs ) Sri B.N. Nitin Kumar on 29 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129173256/
5 may come and snatch the child away.
The aggrieved person has been harassed and tortured physically and mentally by the respondents 1 to 3 since 2003 and continue to be harassed even as on date.
The harassment and torture continue despite having met all their illegal dowry demands.
The aggrieved person has been subjected to cruelty both physical and mental by the respondents 1 to 3 making it impossible for the aggrieved person to stay with the 1st respondent and lead a marital life.
The physical assault, attempts of suicide, filming the aggrieved person, spiking her tea and medicines are all acts of cruelty which makes is impossible for the aggrieved person to live with the 1st respondent.
The aggrieved person has been a victim of domestic violence in the hands of the respondent No.1 to 3.
The aggrieved person has been a victim of domestic violence in the hands of all the respondents.
opennyai_summary.issue:
The following points would arise for my consideration.
1. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the relief's as sought in the petition?
2. What order?
7. On perusal of materials before this court, My findings on the above said points are as under:
1. POINT No.1: PARTLY IN THE AFFIRMATIVE 2. POINT No.2: AS PER FINAL ORDER For the following REASONS 8. POINT No.1:
To file a petition U/s.12 of the Act, it is necessary that the petitioner has to establish two things firstly, she must establish that, the petitioner and respondent or respondents lived or are living together, in a domestic relationship.
Secondly, that the respondent or respondents have subjected her to acts of domestic violence.
To prove the domestic relationship the petitioner is required to prove that she and the respondents have lived together in a relationship of marriage or in a relationship in the nature of marriage or related by consanguinity or adoption or as family members living together as a joint family.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Smt. B.N.A. Shilpa Lakshmi vs ) Sri B.N. Nitin Kumar on 29 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129173256/
9 14.
The petitioners have failed to prove the respondent has harassed them.
However no specific allegations are being made against the respondents so as to prove the act of Domestic Violence.
Mere allegations which are not specific and which are vague in nature cannot be accepted as proof of Domestic Violence.
15. When such being the case, the infliction of domestic violence made against the respondents gets diluted and same cannot be accepted.
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 is beneficiary legislation and is intended to protect the interest of wife.
In order to claim any relief under the said Act, must satisfy and prove before this Court that she is an aggrieved woman U/s.2(a)
of the said Act and she has been subjected to domestic violence as defined U/s.3 of Domestic violence Act.
Hence on perusal of the evidence of P.W.1 it establishes that except the vague allegations made against the respondent No.1, the petitioner has not proved her case of domestic violence against him.
16. The petitioner has sought for a protection order restraining the respondent from committing an act of Domestic Violence.
As discussed above there are no evidence to show that an act of Domestic Violence was committed by the respondent.
Hence this relief is liable to be declined.
17. The petitioner has sought for a residence order U/s.19 of Domestic Violence Act, directing the respondents to secure same level or alternative accommodation for petitioner.
On perusal of materials before this court, there is no evidence placed by the petitioner to prove the level of accommodation she enjoyed while she was residing with the respondent and the shared house hold.
Since the act of Domestic violence is not specifically proved before this Court granting compensation would be inappropriate.
But, the respondent No.1 is held responsible to pay compensation amount of Rs.3,00,000/- as the respondent No.1 being the husband of petitioner, he is also the father of the child.
It is his bound duty to look after the legally wedded wife and child born out of wedlock.
He has to discharge his duty as husband as well as a responsible father.
opennyai_summary.decision:
19. POINT No.2:
In view of the materials placed before this court, pleadings, depositions and documentary evidence, this court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005, is allowed in part.
The protection order U/s.18 of Act is hereby rejected.
The residence order U/s.19 of Act is also rejected.
Further the respondent No.1 is directed to pay to the petitioner Rs.3,00,000/-
(Rupees Three Lakhs) as compensation.
The claim of maintenance for the petitioner is hereby rejected.
The petition as against the respondent No.2 and 3 is hereby dismissed.
No order as to costs.
Office is directed to furnish copy of this order to both the parties at free of cost.
